name: Indian High Court Judgments (AWS Open Data Registry)
publisher: Dattam Labs (community project; source data from eCourts judgments portal)
caveats: High Court matters are bail, quashing and appeal - disposal_nature here is NOT a trial outcome.
description and raw_html columns contain party names and addresses; drop at the ingest boundary.
The PDF corpus was harvested upstream with an ONNX CAPTCHA solver; we consume a published CC-BY dataset but the project should rule on that explicitly.
Registry YAML says UpdateFrequency: Quarterly while the repo CI syncs daily - trust the bucket, not the YAML.
Coverage per court/bench is uneven; see STATS.md for per-court counts.
evidence: Anonymous S3 list of indian-high-court-judgments returned 200 on 2026-09-20 with prefixes data/ and metadata/{json,parquet,parquet_case_details,tar}/. Registry YAML read verbatim from awslabs/open-data-registry: License CC-BY-4.0, ManagedBy Dattam Labs, Contact contact@dattam.in, ARN arn:aws:s3:::indian-high-court-judgments, Region ap-south-1. STATS.md (2026-06-01 snapshot): 17,771,420 PDFs, 17,775,080 metadata records, 1,276.94 GiB, 25 courts, 45 benches, 1950-2026. metadata/parquet schema read from a real file: court_code,title,description,judge,pdf_link,cnr,date_of_registration,decision_date,disposal_nature,court,raw_html,pdf_exists.
how_to_obtain: aws s3 sync s3://indian-high-court-judgments/metadata/parquet/ ./ --no-sign-request, or plain HTTPS GET against the bucket endpoint. No AWS account needed.
notes: The only registered, licensed, national court dataset found. Attribution required under CC-BY-4.0.

name: Indian High Court Judgments - metadata/parquet_case_details (mobile-API dimension table)
geo_coverage: 4 High Courts populated: 23_23 Madhya Pradesh, 27_1 Bombay, 2_5 Himachal Pradesh, 9_13 Allahabad
caveats: Carries fir_no and fir_year but NO police-station name or code column - the FIR cannot be resolved to a thana from this table alone.
Only 4 of 25 High Courts populated as of 2026-09-20; Patna (court=10_8) listing returned empty.
One row per CNR, not year-partitioned; filter date_of_decision for time queries.
Includes cases with no order/judgment, which never appear in the per-order tables.
Party and advocate names present.
evidence: Downloaded metadata/parquet_case_details/court=2_5/bench=cmis/case_details-mobile.parquet (12,449 B, 5 rows) and read the schema: cnr, case_no, case_type, court, bench, judge, bench_name, judicial_section, petitioner, respondent, pet_advocate, res_advocate, date_of_filing, date_of_registration, date_of_decision, disposal_nature, purpose_name, fir_no, fir_year, lower_court, acts list<struct<act,section>>, hearings list<struct<cause_list_type,judge,business_on_date,hearing_date,purpose_of_listing>>, linked_cases, documents, source. Delimiter listing of the prefix returned exactly 4 court partitions.
notes: Derived from the eCourts mobile API, which is why it has fields the website never exposed.

name: Indian District Court Judgments - public S3 pilot bucket (indian-district-court-judgments-test)
geo_coverage: Bucket layout is all-India; only state_code 29 (Telangana) is populated for 2023-2025
caveats: ONE STATE. Listing 2023/, 2024/ and 2025/ with a delimiter returns exactly one state prefix each: 29 (Telangana). Bihar (state 8) is absent.

No AWS Open Data Registry entry (indian-district-court-judgments.yaml returns 404) and NO data licence statement. The repo's MIT licence covers code, not data. Do not redistribute derivatives until a licence exists.
police_st_code is 0 in all 1,966 records sampled; the station survives only as a free-text name inside fir_details, with doubled spaces and PS/P.S. variants.
FIR fill rate varies by court complex: 927/1054 (88%) in one 2023 complex vs 255/912 (28%) in another, same state, same year.
disp_name is court-local free text, not a controlled vocabulary (ADMISSION OF CLAIM dominates a criminal docket).
Party names, advocate names and address fragments are present (pet_name, res_name, pet_adv, res_adv, petNameAdd, resNameAdd).
metadata/parquet/.../cases.parquet is NOT a substitute - it has no FIR and no disposal nature; the join lives in the metadata tar JSONs.
Bucket name ends in -test; treat it as a pilot that could be withdrawn.
evidence: Downloaded 2023/29/1/1290014/metadata.tar (11,479,040 B, 1,054 case JSONs) and 2023/29/22/1290148/metadata.tar (12,533,760 B, 912 JSONs) on 2026-09-20. history block has 92 keys including fir_details, fir_no, fir_year, police_st_code, date_of_filing, dt_regis, date_of_decision, disp_name, disp_nature, under_act1..4, under_sec1..4, act, type_name, court_name, est_code, district_name, state_name. Verified record TSAD090000312023: type CC, date_of_filing 2023-01-17, date_of_decision 2024-03-19, disp_name ACQUITTAL, disp_nature 12, fir_details '41^Excise  Police  Echoda^2022'. Outcome vocabulary observed across both complexes includes CONVICTED, ACQUITTAL, DISCHARGED, COMMITTED TO SESSIONS, COMPROMISED, CLOSED, SETTLED BEFORE LOK ADALAT, QUASHED, TRANSFERRED, ABATED. FIR-year to decision-year lag: median 0, p90 2 (n=471).
how_to_obtain: aws s3 sync s3://indian-district-court-judgments-test/2023/29/ ./ --no-sign-request, or HTTPS GET https://indian-district-court-judgments-test.s3.amazonaws.com/<key>. For any state other than Telangana, or for a data licence, contact Dattam Labs at contact@dattam.in.
notes: THE key finding of this dossier: the FIR-to-court join is obtainable in bulk with no CAPTCHA, because this metadata came from the eCourts mobile API. fir_details parses as FIR_number ^ police_station_name ^ FIR_year.

name: eCourts mobile API (app.ecourts.gov.in/ecourt_mobile_DC) - CAPTCHA-free case docket service
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
caveats: NO CAPTCHA anywhere in the flow - this is the surface that makes the FIR join bulk-obtainable, and it is why the district S3 pilot exists.

Requests and responses are AES-CBC encrypted with keys extracted from the official Android APK; the server presents a self-signed certificate. Not a CAPTCHA (INGESTION.md rule 1 does not fire) but an access control in substance (rule 2 does).
Reported 10-50x faster than the CAPTCHA'd web portal for the same coverage.
No published terms of use for machine access.
evidence: Read mobile/api_client.py verbatim: BASE_URL https://app.ecourts.gov.in/ecourt_mobile_DC, PACKAGE_NAME in.gov.ecourts.eCourtsServices, APP_VERSION 3.0, device uid '<uuid16>:<package>', verify_ssl=False. Endpoints: appReleaseWebService.php, stateWebService.php (action_code=getStates), districtWebService.php, courtEstWebService.php (action_code=fillCourtComplex), caseNumberWebService.php, searchByCaseType.php, caseHistoryWebService.php, getAllLabelsWebService.php, display_pdf.php. The upstream project's own comparison table records 'CAPTCHA per complex/year: 0' for mobile vs ~32 for web, and 'FIR number / police station: mobile API only'.
how_to_obtain: Do not run it. Consume the published S3 output (case-outcomes-aws-dc-judgments-pilot) instead; for unmirrored states, ask Dattam Labs or the High Court Registrar (Computer Cell).
notes: RECOMMENDATION: excluded on terms-of-use grounds, not CAPTCHA grounds. Recorded so the decision is explicit and reviewable.

name: eCourts web portal - home/viewHistory case enrichment (no CAPTCHA)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
caveats: Returns acts, sections, case status, case stage, decision date and full hearing history but NOT the FIR block - FIR is mobile-API-only.
Requires internal_case_no + cnr + court_code, which come from a CAPTCHA'd search or from another dataset.
Hearing-history table parses to garbled dict keys in the reference implementation; needs its own parser.
No published machine-access terms.
evidence: WEB_SCRAPER_REFERENCE.md documents 'Phase 2 - Case Enrichment (NO CAPTCHA)' with a field table marking Yes for CNR, filing/registration date, decision date, first/next hearing, case status and stage, court number and judge, parties and advocates, acts and sections, full hearing history; and No (mobile API only) for Hindi transliterations and FIR number/police station. Its cost model lists 'Enrich 1 case (viewHistory): 0 CAPTCHAs'.
how_to_obtain: init_session() once per complex (2 lightweight HTTP calls, no CAPTCHA), then POST ?p=home/viewHistory per case with internal_case_no, cnr, court_code.
notes: Corrects an earlier assumption that every eCourts endpoint is CAPTCHA-gated. Discovery is gated; enrichment is not.

name: eCourts casestatus/fillPoliceStation - national police-station option list (no CAPTCHA)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
caveats: No geometry, no lat/lon - a name and a code only.
One station appears under every court establishment whose jurisdiction covers it; deduplicate.
Names are uppercase free text with PS/P.S. variants and will not exactly match the fir_details strings in the district S3 records.
Whether uniform_code equals the CCTNS/NCRB uniform police-station code is still unverified.
evidence: WEB_PORTAL_SEARCH_OPTIONS.md (dated 2026-04-28, written against live POSTs) records: POST ?p=casestatus/fillPoliceStation with state_code, dist_code, court_complex_code, est_code, ajax_req=true, app_token returns {"police_station_list": "<option value='2-33325003'>Arjunda 2</option>...", "status": 1, "app_token": ...}. 7 stations returned at Civil Court Gunderdehi (state=18, district=19, complex=1180084). Explicitly listed under 'CAPTCHA-Free Helper Endpoints'.
how_to_obtain: GET a tab to obtain SERVICES_SESSID and app_token, POST casestatus/set_data to bind the complex, then POST fillPoliceStation. One request per complex; 3,567 complexes nationally. Single-threaded with a delay, per INGESTION.md rule 4.
notes: Reference data, not case data - far lower risk than case scraping, and it is the only route to a stable station key for blocker 3.

name: Development Data Lab - Indian Judicial Data (81M district court cases, 2010-2018)
geo_coverage: all-India district and subordinate courts, including Bihar
caveats: CONFIRMED: no FIR number and no police station. Neither appears in any downstream loader's column list, dtype map or merge key; party names were replaced by gender flags in the same anonymisation step.
BUT cino IS the raw 16-character CNR (observed MHNB030013812010), so the FIR link is re-joinable per case against the mobile-API/S3 records - it was stripped, not destroyed.
Series stops in 2018 and is entirely pre-BNS.
act_key is unnormalised free text: five separate codes exist for the Motor Vehicles Act alone.
disp_name is an integer that must be resolved through disp_name_key on (disp_name, year).
District IDs predate roughly eight years of district creation and need remapping.
Non-commercial licence with ShareAlike; a commercial map needs a separate licence from DDL.
evidence: devdatalab.org and dropbox.com are egress-blocked here. File layout and the complete column list were read from three independent downstream projects on GitHub. cases_YYYY columns: ddl_case_id, year, state_code, dist_code, court_no, cino, judge_position, female_defendant, female_petitioner, female_adv_def, female_adv_pet, type_name, purpose_name, disp_name, date_of_filing, date_of_decision, date_first_list, date_last_list, date_next_list. acts_sections: ddl_case_id, act, section, bailable_ipc, number_sections_ipc, criminal. Keys: act_key, section_key, disp_name_key(disp_name,year->disp_name_s,count), type_name_key, purpose_name_key, cases_state_key, cases_district_key, cases_court_key, judge_case_merge_key. Observed cino values MHNB030013812010, MHNB030004552010 - valid CNR format. WebSearch confirmed 81.2M cases, ~10M criminal, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
how_to_obtain: Download the csv/ or dta/ subfolder from the Dropbox link on devdatalab.org/judicial-data. For extended or de-anonymised access, apply to DDL as a researcher.
notes: Answers the brief directly: disposition YES (disp_name), disposal date YES (date_of_decision), FIR/police station NO - previous agent confirmed. The new finding is cino.

name: DDL replication package - In-group Bias in the Indian Judiciary (criminal subset)
publisher: Development Data Lab / Ash, Asher, Bhowmick, Chen, Devi, Goessman, Novosad, Siddiqi
caveats: NOT anonymised: the build scripts reference def_name, pet_name, pet_adv, def_adv, judge_desg, state_name, district_name, court_name. Do not ingest the name-bearing files.
Ships a name-to-religion/gender classifier. Applying it to a public crime map would be indefensible; do not.
Needs ~30 GB RAM and Stata 16+ to rebuild.
Criminal subset only (~24.51M obs before filtering, 5M analysis sample).
evidence: README.md read from github: files cases_clean_2010..2018.dta, judges_clean.dta, poi_master.dta, ACLED_India_violence_2005-2023.csv, acled_districts, and keys/ containing acled_district_key, cases_district_key, cases_state_key, disp_name_key, pc11_court_district_key, purpose_name_key, type_name_key. table_sample_representativeness.do starts from ~24.51 million obs and drops ~31K for missing def_name.
how_to_obtain: Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/GHLGSW (stable) or the Google Drive link in the repo README.
notes: Worth it only for keys/pc11_court_district_key.dta, a court-district to PC11 census-code crosswalk we need anyway.

name: NCRB Crime in India - Disposal of Crime Cases by Police
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: State/UT and the 19 metropolitan cities ONLY. There is no district disposal table and no police-station disposal table anywhere in the public record.
Chargesheeting rate is computed over cases DISPOSED by police after investigation, not over cases registered - a denominator trap that inflates the apparent rate.
Principal offence rule: a case is counted once, under its gravest head.
The 'final report false - mistake of fact/law' bucket is where police non-action hides, and it is only ever published as a state total.
IPC to BNS break at 2024-07-01 makes 2024 onward non-comparable at crime-head level.
evidence: ncrb.gov.in and data.gov.in both egress-blocked this session. Search results confirm the published series titles 'Disposal of IPC Crime Cases by Police' (indiastat mirror) and the data.gov.in resource 'Crime Head-wise Police Disposal of Indian Penal Code (IPC) Crimes in Metropolitan Cities during 2022'. Disposal categories confirmed as: charge-sheeted; final report submitted (true but untraced/no clue/insufficient evidence; false - mistake of fact, mistake of law, civil dispute); withdrawn by government; pending investigation. Reported national IPC chargesheeting rate 75.8% (2020), 72.7% (2023). A 2020 figure cited from Table 4A.3 (crimes against children): of 1,29,820 cases disposed by police, final report in 44,485 and charge sheet in 85,185.
how_to_obtain: Download the Crime in India volume PDFs and the matching data.gov.in CSV resources from an unblocked, India-resident network. Table numbers must be re-verified there - I will not guess them.
notes: The ONLY public record of a case being closed by police rather than by a court. It is the reason a court-derived thana map is structurally blind to police non-action.

name: NCRB Crime in India - Disposal of Crime Cases by Courts
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: State/UT and metropolitan city only; no district or police-station breakdown.
Conviction rate denominator is trials completed, not cases registered - it is not comparable to a court-record-derived rate without restating both.
Principal offence rule applies.
IPC to BNS break at 2024-07-01.
evidence: Series title 'Disposal of IPC Crime Cases by Courts' confirmed via the indiastat mirror path /data/crime-and-law/disposal-of-ipc-crime-cases-by-courts. Categories: trials completed, convicted, discharged, acquitted, cases withdrawn, pending trial, conviction rate. NCRB host blocked this session.
how_to_obtain: Same as the police disposal tables.
notes: This is the benchmark our court-derived thana rollups must reconcile to. If a Telangana rollup does not match the NCRB Telangana state total, the extraction is wrong.

name: Dataful and Indiastat mirrors of the NCRB disposal tables
caveats: Adds no granularity over NCRB - it only saves PDF-table extraction effort.
Freemium/paid; redistribution restricted by terms.
Derived data: any NCRB revision propagates with a lag.
evidence: dataful.in is egress-blocked; search results confirm dataset 458 'NCRB: Police disposal of cases of fake/false news and rumours registered under Section 505 of IPC' and collection 1108 'NCRB Crime in India (Summary)'. Indiastat paths for both disposal series returned as search results.
how_to_obtain: Paid subscription to either. Evaluate only if PDF extraction proves more expensive than the licence.

name: Patna High Court FIR-in-caption extraction (Bihar thana-keyed outcomes)
publisher: Patna High Court, via the AWS Indian High Court Judgments corpus
caveats: NOT trial outcomes. 63% of FIR-linked rows are BAIL GRANTED or BAIL REJECTED. Labelling this 'case closed' would be false.

Thana strings include non-geographic entries: Excise P.S. (3,310), MAHILA P.S. (1,034) plus MAHILA PS (537), PATNA COMPLAINT CASE (1,002), SC/ST (551), COMPLAINT CASE (504), GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL COMP. (438).
26% of 2024 rows have no parsable block (civil writs, service matters).
Junk FIR years occur - one lag of -999 observed; filter on 1990 <= fir_year <= decision_year.
The caption is a registry clerk's free text, not a CIS field; format can change without notice. Re-measure the match rate on every refresh.
Patna-specific. Other High Courts do not share this convention (unverified for the other 24).
description text contains party names and home addresses.
evidence: Downloaded year=2024/court=10_8/bench=patnahcucisdb94/metadata.parquet on 2026-09-20: 123,106 rows. Caption example: 'CRIMINAL MISCELLANEOUS No.83783 of 2023 Arising Out of PS. Case No.-136 Year-2023 Thana- CHHATAUNI District- East Champaran'. Regex over description matched 90,988 rows (73.9%), yielding 1,225 distinct thana strings across 51 districts. Top districts Patna 8,849, East Champaran 5,830, Gaya 5,004, Saran 4,190, Samastipur 3,902, Madhubani 3,584, Vaishali 3,484, Muzaffarpur 3,304. disposal_nature for FIR-linked rows: BAIL GRANTED 51,674, ALLOWED 14,431, WITHDRAWN 6,641, DISMISSED 5,802, BAIL REJECTED 5,687, DISPOSED 4,127. FIR-year to decision-year lag median 1, p90 5. STATS.md records 1,692,461 Patna HC PDFs / 1,692,492 metadata records / 90.28 GiB.
notes: The only thana-keyed Bihar court data that exists in public today. Ship it as a clearly-labelled BAIL layer, never as a crime-outcome layer.

name: Bihar district-court case outcomes - confirmed absent from every public source
caveats: Bihar (state_code 8) has no partition in the public district-court bucket for any year.
DDL covers Bihar but only to district x act x section x disposition, 2010-2018.
Justice Hub's CALPRA-1986 dataset includes Bihar but is a single statute, 10,800 cases, 2015-2023.
Bihar's own scrb.bihar.gov.in FIR repository is the input side only - no outcome field.
evidence: Listed s3://indian-district-court-judgments-test with delimiter for 2023/, 2024/, 2025/: each returned exactly one CommonPrefix, state 29. Explicit listing of 2023/8/ and 2024/8/ returned no common prefixes and no keys.
how_to_obtain: Either (a) ask Dattam Labs (contact@dattam.in) to run their existing mobile pipeline for state_code 8, or (b) write to the Registrar (Computer Cell), Patna High Court, requesting a de-identified extract of case master plus FIR fields for the Bihar district judiciary, citing DDL's release as precedent and offering to publish only aggregates.
notes: This is the specific gap that decides whether Bihar gets a real 'case closed' thana layer. Absence verified, not assumed.

name: National Judicial Data Grid v3 - district and High Court pendency/disposal dashboards
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC / Department of Justice
geo_coverage: all-India (18,735 district and subordinate courts plus High Courts)
caveats: Stock and flow, not crime counts. Pendency is not incidence.
Civil/criminal split only; no crime-head detail and no police station.
Snapshot semantics - no history is retained, so a time series exists only if we start snapshotting daily.
URLs carry a rotating app_token; the v3 path replaced njdgnew.
The NJDG Open API is restricted to Central and State Government departmental IDs; public extension is only 'proposed'.
evidence: njdg.ecourts.gov.in egress-blocked this session. Search returned live v3 URLs of the form https://njdg.ecourts.gov.in/njdg_v3//?p=home%2Findex&state_code=28%7E2&app_token=<64hex> and the High Court view at /hcnjdg_v2/, confirming the v3/v2 path rename since the previous dossier.
how_to_obtain: Daily cron snapshot of the district dashboard, stored as dated rows. For the API, apply to the Department of Justice for a departmental ID and access key via an institutional partner.
notes: Only useful as a denominator and a freshness check; it can never produce a thana.

name: openjustice-in/ecourts - eCourts field-schema reference and committed fixtures
geo_coverage: all-India High Courts (district coverage stated as in development)
caveats: GPL-3.0-or-later: linking it into our pipeline has licence consequences for anything we distribute.
High Court oriented; the FIR block is frequently null at High Court level - 150+ committed J&K fixtures all have fir: null.
Its own README disclaims legal responsibility for anyone running it.
Single-threaded by design; adopt that ethic regardless of whether we use the code.
evidence: Read entities/fir.py (FIR: state, district, police_station, number, year), entities/case.py (Case: case_type, registration_number, cnr_number, filing_number, registration_date, first_hearing_date, decision_date, case_status, nature_of_disposal, coram, bench, state, district, judicial, petitioners, respondents, orders, case_number, hearings, category, sub_category, objections, not_before_me, filing_date, fir, token) and parsers/case_details.py, which reads span.FIR_details_table into State/District/Police Station/FIR Number/Year and the Case Status block into First Hearing Date, Decision Date, Nature of Disposal, Coram, Bench, Not Before Me. Fixture test/fixtures/case_details/KAHC010337682024.yml re-verified: fir {state KARNATAKA, district BENGALURU, police_station 'INDIRANAGAR PS', number '155', year 2024}, case_status ORDERS, filing_date 2024-06-14, registration_date 2024-06-18.
how_to_obtain: pip install ecourts, or read the source for the schema without taking the GPL dependency.
notes: Use as documentation of the record shape; do not link the GPL code into a distributed pipeline without a licence review.

name: vanga/indian-district-court-judgments - eCourts scraper and endpoint documentation (reference only)
geo_coverage: all-India district and taluka courts (3,567 court complexes, 36 states/UTs)
caveats: Ships web/src/captcha_solver/captcha.onnx, an ONNX CAPTCHA solver. INGESTION.md rule 1 forbids us running this.
Its own cost model: full national first pass ~680,000 CAPTCHAs, 2-4 weeks at 2 workers.
case_status parameters must be the full words Pending/Disposed/Both; P/D/B silently returns 'Record not found'.
courts.csv ships a pre-generated hierarchy of 3,567 complexes, which is useful reference data on its own.
evidence: Read README.md, web/WEB_PORTAL_SEARCH_OPTIONS.md (dated 2026-04-28, all seven casestatus search tabs with live-tested parameters and measured result counts) and web/WEB_SCRAPER_REFERENCE.md (the CAPTCHA vs no-CAPTCHA endpoint split and the cost model). Documents the full ajaxCall contract: GET tab for SERVICES_SESSID + app_token, POST casestatus/set_data, GET vendor/securimage/securimage_show.php, POST the submit endpoint with ajax_req=true and a rotating app_token, parse JSON with status/div_captcha/app_token plus case_data|party_data|adv_data|act_data|filing_data.
how_to_obtain: Read the documentation; do not run the scraper. Consume the S3 output instead.
notes: Best public map of the eCourts surface. Kept as a reference entry precisely so the reason we are not running it is recorded.

name: Indian Supreme Court Judgments (AWS Open Data Registry)
caveats: National granularity; no geography below the court itself.
Relevant only for validating outcome definitions and for doctrine.
evidence: awslabs/open-data-registry/datasets/indian-supreme-court-judgments.yaml returned HTTP 200 (contents not read). Search results confirm 1950-2025 coverage and CC-BY-4.0.

name: Justice Hub / DAKSH / CivicDataLab curated eCourts outcome datasets
geo_coverage: selected states per dataset (POCSO: Assam, Delhi, Haryana; CALPRA: Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, UP)
caveats: Single-statute slices, not general crime coverage.
Justice Hub host is egress-blocked here; contents confirmed only from a prior dossier and from CivicDataLab's own project page.
Whether any of them retain the FIR block is unverified.
evidence: justicehub.in blocked this session. CivicDataLab's repository civicdatalab.github.io contains content/work/lawandjustice/trackingpocso/index.md, which matched a search for the phrase 'Disposal of Cases by Police' - the POCSO tracker methodology. Dataset descriptions (POCSO 19,783 cases; CALPRA 10,800 cases Jan 2015-Mar 2023 across six states including Bihar) carried forward from research/sources/judiciary-prisons.md.
how_to_obtain: Download from justicehub.in/dataset from an unblocked network; DAKSH's database is on request.
notes: Read the POCSO methodology before writing any act-specific extractor - it is the best published worked example.
